title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Studying, Publicizing, and Implementing the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Learning, Publicizing, and Implementing
the Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China

Fa Fa [1992] No. 37

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army, and all Maritime Courts:

The Maritime Code of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Maritime Code) has been adopted at the 28th Session of the Standing Committee of the Seventh National People's Congress and shall come into force on July 1, 1993. The Maritime Code is the basic standard for regulating maritime transport relationships and ship relationships, and it constitutes the legal basis for people's courts in adjudicating maritime and maritime-related cases. Its enactment and implementation represent a significant event in the construction of China's maritime legal system and will play an important role in perfecting and enhancing the socialist maritime legal system, protecting the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese and foreign parties, and promoting the development of China's maritime transport industry and economic and trade undertakings. For the purpose of correctly implementing and enforcing the Maritime Code, the following notice is hereby given:

1. People's courts at all levels, especially the maritime courts and the courts of their appellate instance, shall seize the time and earnestly organize the trial personnel to study the Maritime Code. The Maritime Code is a special civil law formulated based on China's national conditions and the characteristics of maritime transport. It is based on currently prevailing international conventions, incorporates private rules reflecting international customs, and draws on widely influential standard contracts; therefore, it is a domestic law with strong international character. We must not only study the legal provisions article by article and chapter by chapter, but also study the relevant international conventions in order to deepen our understanding. The Supreme People's Court will hold a training course on the Maritime Code in early next year to train leading cadres in maritime trial work. Thereafter, each maritime court shall organize its own training sessions, or adopt methods such as meeting-based training, to train all maritime trial personnel. Through such study, they shall deeply comprehend the legislative spirit of the articles of the Maritime Code, accurately grasp the legal provisions, focus on key points, and thoroughly learn and understand them.

2. People's courts at all levels shall, in light of local actual conditions and in active cooperation with relevant departments, extensively and in-depth carry out publicity activities on the Maritime Code, so that the broad masses of the people can understand and comply with the Maritime Code, correctly exercise their civil rights, actively fulfill their civil obligations, and resolve maritime and maritime-related disputes in accordance with the law. The publicity of the Maritime Code shall focus on key points, be targeted, and emphasize practical results. It is necessary to combine the handling of cases in accordance with the law with publicity efforts, and by adjudicating typical cases and explaining the law through cases, expand the publicity effect so that the Maritime Code truly becomes deeply rooted in the hearts of the people.

3. After the Maritime Code comes into force, people's courts at all levels must strictly implement it. For maritime transport relationships and ship relationships that occur after the Maritime Code comes into force, the Maritime Code shall be applied in adjudication. For maritime and maritime-related cases that were accepted before the Maritime Code comes into force but have not yet been concluded after it comes into force, or for maritime transport relationships and ship relationships that occurred before the Maritime Code comes into force but where the parties file an action after it comes into force, the relevant provisions in force at the time shall be applied in adjudication; where there were no provisions at that time, the matter may be handled by reference to the Maritime Code.

4. With respect to maritime and maritime-related cases that have been finally adjudicated by the people's court before the Maritime Code comes into force, if after the Maritime Code comes into force the parties apply for a retrial and the case is retried under the trial supervision procedure, the relevant provisions in force at the time of the conclusion of the original trial shall apply.

5. For cases involving disputes over cargo transport contracts arising during coastal transport and maritime and maritime-related cases arising during inland water transport, the relevant laws and regulations such as the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and the Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China shall still apply.

6. People's courts at all levels must adhere to strict enforcement of the law. After the Maritime Code comes into force, the previous provisions and interpretations made by the Supreme People's Court regarding substantive adjudication of maritime and maritime-related cases, to the extent that they conflict with the Maritime Code, shall no longer be applied. In the process of implementing and enforcing the Maritime Code, it is necessary to strengthen investigation and research. For important and difficult issues concerning the application of law encountered during implementation, such issues shall be promptly summarized and reported to our court so that our court may, on the basis of the provisions and legislative spirit of the Maritime Code and by summarizing the experience of maritime trial practice, propose opinions on several issues concerning the implementation and enforcement of the Maritime Code.

November 18, 1992
